rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF RICHARD E. ANDERSON
rulings.Calendar Matter: Petition For Instructions, Accounting, And Order Compelling Distribution
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 10/13/26. (No earlier availability.) Issue(s) necessitating continuance: (1) No proposed order has been lodged or received by the assigned examiner. [LRSF 14.7 A. and 14.59 E.] (2) Notice must have attached to it the procedures for how to make a remote appearance by Zoom and CourtCall, as well as remote public access, as set out at https://sf.courts.ca.gov/divisions/probate-court. [LRSF 14.1 C.6.] Please provide a proposed order and a courtesy copy of the proof of service of notice of the 10/13/26 hearing, which has a printout of the instructions for how to appear remotely attached to the notice, to the assigned examiner by 9/29/26. Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B. NOTE: The fiduciary is Charles Anderson, who was appointed as the administrator and has apparently not yet completed distribution, as ordered on 7/31/23. After all the 13100 affidavits were finally filed, he simply needed to distribute the $130,110.93 (calculated as of 3/31/22) that had been set aside for Renella Anderson to the remaining 10 heirs, who are her also heirs-at-law. Administrator was also directed to file a supplemental account, because assets on hand in his accounting were not all cash but included Treasury bills. He was permitted to submit the accounting via an ex parte petition that also sought payment of his and his attorney's remaining statutory compensation ($10,000 each). Administrator was also authorized to retain a $20,000 reserve (in addition to the $20,000 balance of statutory compensation reserved until all of this was done, the estate finally distributed, and the ex parte petition with his supplemental accounting was filed). This petition should not have been necessary but for Administrator's and his attorney's failure to complete distribution and file the ex parte petition with the supplemental accounting for the period following 3/31/22 until the estate was finally distributed and to request payment of the rest of their statutory compensation.

rulings.Case Title: IN THE MATTER OF THE IN RE THE 2004 MALEK-ZADEH FAMILY TRUST DATED JANUARY 23, 2004
rulings.Calendar Matter: Petition For Order Confirming Assets Of Trust Under Cal Prob Code 850
rulings.Rulings: Hearing. Appearance required. The judicial officer is to review and determine: 1) Does Probate Code section 15200(a), the only legal basis for section 850 relief cited in this petition, apply to unknown property the settlors may or may not acquire after executing the trust instrument including a schedule of trust assets? Section 15200(a) states that a trust can be created by a declaration by the owner of property that the owner "holds" (present tense) the property as trustee, but not by a declaration that the owner "will hold" or "may hold in the future". "General Assignment of Trust Ownership" signed by the settlors in this case states that the settlors are "now holding and will continue to hold" everything as trust assets. While the General Assignment purports to cover unknown assets the settlors may "acquire in the future", they are not assets the settlors are "now holding and will continue to hold" in trust. 2) Does section 15200(b) apply to unknown property the settlors may or may not acquire in the future, and if so, can section 15200(b), though not cited in the petition, be an alternative legal basis for the same relief sought by this petition? The General Assignment appears to be a declaration by the owner of property that the owner holds the property as trustee contemplated by section 15200(a), rather than a transfer of property by the owner during the owner's lifetime to another person as trustee contemplated by section 15200(b), as there is no language in the General Assignment such as "assign", "transfer", or "convey", despite the document title indicating otherwise. Article 2.3 of the trust states that additional property becomes part of the trust estate "upon written acceptance of it by the trustee" and requires any additions to the trust to be made by "designating in writing the property to be added". See also Kucker v. Kucker (2011) 192 Cal.App.4th 90 ["Some practitioners have clients periodically assign all (or substantially all) assets to the trust so that a Heggstad petition can be used to capture any overlooked items. A form provided by the practice guide for use when the client has assumed full responsibility for funding the trust can be modified to advise the client to return periodically to execute a general assignment of all or substantially all of their assets to the trust so that a Heggstad petition can be used to capture any later acquired items not titled in the name of the trust."] PARTIES APPEARING SHOULD CHECK IN FOR THE HEARING WITH THEIR FULL NAME. rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF CURT THEISEN
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR PROBATE OF WILL AND FOR LETTERS TESTAMENTARY
rulings.Rulings: Hearing. Appearance required. PARTIES APPEARING SHOULD CHECK IN FOR THE HEARING WITH THEIR FULL NAME. Counsel and parties may appear personally or remotely through Zoom or CourtCall. For a video appearance, go to zoom.us, click "join a meeting" and input meeting ID 160 225 4765 and password 514879. For an audio-only appearance through Zoom, call 1-669-254-5252 and key in meeting ID "160 225 4765#", then participant ID "0#", then password "514879#". (Toll rates may apply).) The Court prefers that counsel and parties appearing by video input their first and last name into the "Your Name" dialogue box. Counsel and parties may appear by audio-only telephone through CourtCall by calling 1-888-882-6878. Please review LRSF 14.1(C) for more information.

rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF JEREMIAH J. GUERIN
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION WITH WILL ANNEXED
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 10/13/26. (No earlier availability.) Issue(s) necessitating continuance: (1) Notice must have attached to it the procedures for how to make a remote appearance by Zoom and CourtCall, as well as remote public access, as set out at https://sf.courts.ca.gov/divisions/probate-court. [LRSF 14.1 C.6.] (2) A proof of holographic instrument is more persuasive if verified by someone other than the petitioner (and his spouse). [LRSF 14.18 A.] Please provide a courtesy copy of any papers filed to address these issues to the assigned examiner by 9/29/26. Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B. NB: Notice of Remote Appearance is not required for Probate matters generally. [LRSF 14.1 C.1.a.]

rulings.Case Title: IN RE: ZARAH CARPENTER
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION TO ESTABLISH FACT OF BIRTH
rulings.Rulings: **UPDATED 8/24/2026 at 9:39 a.m.** Continued to 9/16/2026 per the judge after reviewing the file. (1) The records do not provide sufficient information for the Court to establish the facts related to the birth. No proof or supporting declarations have been submitted. If any witnesses, such as a midwife or another individual, were present at the birth, their verified declarations would be necessary. (2) Clarification of the year of the birth - whether 2025 or 2026. Declaration #4 states 2026.
